title: Permissions, decoded
subtitle: Read mode strings, set least privilege, and know when ACLs are the honest answer.
objectives: Decode a long listing into owner, group, and other permissions
Change modes with symbolic and octal chmod
Set ownership and reason about directory execute bits
Use ACLs and recognize sticky, setgid, and setuid bits

commands.desc: Show type, mode, owner, group, and size.
Add execute permission for the owner.
Show the current default permission mask.
Grant a named user read/write via ACL.
Make new files inherit the directory group.

lab.title: Build a shared project directory
lab.scenario: Two groups need controlled access to one directory. Solve it without 777 and without changing the whole filesystem.

steps.text: Create a shared directory, two groups, and a builder user.
steps.cmd: sudo mkdir -p /srv/fieldbook && sudo groupadd builders && sudo groupadd auditors && sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash builder && sudo usermod -aG builders builder
steps.verify: groupadd and useradd should succeed; id builder should show the builders group.

steps.text: Set ownership and a group-readable/writable mode.
steps.verify: ls -ld /srv/fieldbook should show drwxrws--- and the setgid s.

steps.text: Create a file as a member of builders and confirm group inheritance.
steps.verify: The owner should be builder and the group should be builders, not the user primary group.

steps.text: Grant auditors read access with an ACL instead of changing the mode.
steps.verify: getfacl should show group:auditors:r-- on report.txt without changing the base mode.

steps.text: Verify the base mode, ACL, and effective access.
steps.verify: A + appears after the mode. The ACL lists auditors with r--.

quiz.why: 7 = rwx, 5 = r-x, 0 = none. Owner gets rwx, group r-x, others nothing.

quiz.q: Why can a directory with mode 600 prevent access to a file inside it even if the file is world-readable?
options: Directory execute permission is needed to traverse it
quiz.why: To reach a known path inside a directory, you need execute (search) permission on the directory.

quiz.q: What is the standard way to let two groups share write access without making a directory world-writable?
options: set an ACL for the second group
quiz.why: ACLs grant additional named users or groups precisely. 777 gives everyone write access and hides the design.
